mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is associated with positive 20-day forward S&P 500 returns due to compressed discount rates and accommodative monetary policy, as observed in historical data where FEDFUNDS below 0.5% consistently precedes positive equity returns.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%, or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 235.0 signals persistent inflation, leading to negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns as central banks tighten policy and risk premiums rise.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 235.0, or the rank correlation between CPIAUCSL and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When labor market strength (PAYEMS) and housing market activity (HOUST) both exceed their 12-month moving averages, it indicates robust economic growth without overheating, leading to positive 20-day forward S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings and risk appetite improve.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of instances where both PAYEMS and HOUST exceed their 12-month moving averages, or the interaction term in a regression of returns on PAYEMS and HOUST is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (e.g., FEDFUNDS rising), the S&P 500 experiences negative 20-day forward returns due to increased discount rates, reduced liquidity, and heightened risk aversion as central banks combat inflation.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles (defined by FEDFUNDS rising > 0.1% in 3 months), or the rank correlation between FEDFUNDS and returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 5.0%) signals a weak labor market, leading to negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns as economic growth stalls and corporate earnings face downward pressure.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or the rank correlation between UNRATE and 20-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) is rising above 100.0 and inflation (CPIAUCSL) is below 230.0, it indicates a strong economy without excessive inflation, leading to positive 20-day forward S&P 500 returns as growth and stability support equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO exceeds 100.0 and CPIAUCSL is below 230.0, or the interaction term in a regression of returns on INDPRO and CPIAUCSL is not statistically significant (p>0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 800.0 thousand signals weakening demand, leading to negative 5-day forward S&P 500 returns as economic activity slows and risk aversion increases.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where HOUST falls below 800.0, or the rank correlation between HOUST and 5-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 signals economic contraction, leading to negative 60-day forward S&P 500 returns as recession risks rise and corporate earnings deteriorate.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO falls below 100.0, or the rank correlation between INDPRO and 60-day returns is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
